dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Columbina, are you okay? You look a bit out of sorts.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you two. I'm alright...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Is she thinking about the moon again...?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there anything we can do to help?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's okay! Just tell us! Even if it's something small, you'll feel much better once it's off your chest.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I... would like to try a drink from the tavern.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...What!?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...*sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sorry... Paimon was just a little surprised. You never talk about wanting things for yourself, so...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And, that's it? Just... a drink?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What, were you expecting her to think bigger?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, kinda. At least something a bit more monumental... Like, "Bring me the moon."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, on second thought, it does kinda make sense. Columbina can't go wherever she wants right now, so a trip to the tavern might as well be a trip to the moon...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It's not just how things are now. Even back when I was with the Fatui, when there was no order to capture me... everyone still kept their distance whenever I went out for a walk.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Third of the Fatui Harbingers... That title alone is enough to scare off people who don't know her.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a sec, come to think of it... Maybe this isn't as hard as Paimon first thought...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #A tavern is kind of out of the question, but a drink... Now, that we can do! {NICKNAME}'s got this!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Really?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, but don't set your expectations too high...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Any flavor preferences?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Flavor...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I don't have much experience ordering drinks, so I'm not sure where to start...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Perhaps something that isn't too... heavy?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Umm, what do you mean by "heavy"?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Heavy like... a Fatui overcoat.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That comparison makes it even more confusing...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what do you think?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It reminds me of a time long, long ago, when I was living with the Frostmoon Scions...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The people used to make a kind of tea brewed with fresh mint leaves, spices, and dried berries.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Whenever I passed by their homes, there was always a subtle herbal aroma wafting from the windows...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did you ever get to try it?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I wanted to, but never got the chance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, why not...?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: When a "Goddess" arrives at your door and asks, "May I try your tea?"... No one dares to offer up the "rustic tea" thrown together for their own consumption...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah... Yeah.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: What I received in the end was more like an "offering" for the divine, complete with ornate packaging and all.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Not that it tasted bad, per se... But, it was missing that sense of... "home."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, now we can fix that!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Mmm...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The flavor is delightful.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Though I must say, the idea of adding milk seems quite unorthodox to me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, well this is a Mondstadt recipe. People love adding milk, cream, and sugar to their tea over there.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It's novel... but in a good way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, glad you like it!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Mm... Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It seems moonlight is not the only medium through which one can glimpse the past. Even something as simple as the aroma of a drink can bring back long-forgotten memories...
